reviewerOrPass: Worker A, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: After freezing and replaying the record, reread the annual roster and example sequence, then recalculated 60 plus 80 plus 15 plus 15 plus 10 EC. Rechecked the clinic and two capstone course entry requirements against the source catalogues. Reconsidered the legal content and limits of each finished UCR plan from its underlying course evidence and confirmed that the comparison reserves Dutch legal drafting, advocacy and the later doctrinal sequence to OU. This is a separate same-AI pass.
findings: The regular Dutch-taught part-time LLB is distinct from the Open Bachelor. The 2026–27 study guide year roster confirms 60 EC of introductory study, 80 EC of later compulsory courses, a 15 EC internal minor, 15 EC of open electives and the 10 EC final assignment. The 10 EC introductory criminal law course and ten 5 EC units account for the introductory phase. The 2026–27 guide separates introductory obligations and property law into distinct 5 EC components. The guide’s annual roster places Rechtswinkel first and the public-law essay first, which defines the choices illustrated here. Programme-page prose lists the minors in a different order, but does not designate a default; the ordered cohort roster is used for this illustration. The clinic is optional within the required internal-minor choice. The entrepreneur and public enforcement minors corroborate the two adjacent directions. The entrepreneur minor’s employment and social-security strand is corroborated by both sources; the two sources differ in naming its first commercial course, which is outside the selected example.

Introductory law is recommended first and enrollment in it precedes registration for introductory EU law. Advanced contracts require enrollment in introductory obligations and property. Substantive criminal law requires completion of introductory criminal law, and Selected Topics in Criminal Law requires substantive criminal law and criminal procedure. The example plans leave room for a 12-month clinic after the 60 EC introductory phase, six specified 5 EC courses and one further eligible 5 EC course, for 95 EC. The 5 EC public-law essay and 5 EC advocacy practicum each require 140 earned EC and completion of or enrollment in their respective specified courses. Essay preparation requires both advanced administrative courses, both criminal law courses, EU law and International Law. The practicum requires contract, liability, property, civil procedure, both administrative and both criminal courses. The guide and model schedules keep the advanced compulsory work and finals in a compatible order; pace is flexible.

The closest plan includes all seven UCR law courses, from foundations and rights through private, criminal, constitutional, public international and EU law. Ethics, negotiation, argument, social science and economics support how the law works in society. The public plan shifts five courses toward modern and imperial history, social theory, environmental movements and comparative policy analysis, with substantive weight on public institutions across legal systems. It offers EU, constitutional and international law and historical and policy inquiry; it does not substitute for Dutch administrative procedure, public enforcement or a legal clinic. The commercial plan adds transnational business law and keeps private and EU law, with finance, accounting, international trade and organizational study. AI ethics supplies privacy, fairness and accountability within the digital strand, without being a technology-law survey. Across the plans, empirical and historical research methods complement legal interpretation; legal drafting, Dutch procedural doctrine, supervised clinic work and courtroom advocacy remain materially different. The six positive alignments reflect shared areas of legal subject matter, and the other cells distinguish complements from counterparts.
